existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchSubject` has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns are the incompatible required `status` binding and semantics, the required `individual`→`subject` element rename with widened reference targets, and the lossy replacement of arm strings with `comparisonGroup`. The main uncertainty is how HL7 intended implementations to map existing subject lifecycle states into R6 publication status plus the new lifecycle backbone elements.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat R6 `ResearchSubject` as a remodeled resource, not just an additive version bump. R4 data needs explicit transforms for required fields (`individual` to `subject`, `status` to some combination of R6 `status` and `subjectState`) and policy decisions for data that R4 cannot carry (`subjectState`, `subjectMilestone`, non-patient subjects, multiple consents, and coded/reference comparison groups). Generated models and FHIRPath/search logic that assume R4 paths will need direct updates.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, reference-target, and required-binding changes because they are present in the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and related local CodeSystems. Confidence is lower for authorial intent and exact terminology migration because no official diff, standalone narrative migration guide, or external THO expansions for the new example-bound state/milestone value sets were available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
ResearchSubject keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 3 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 3 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 43/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

2 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Required `individual` was renamed to required `subject` and widened beyond Patient
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances carry `individual` and lack required R6 `subject`; R6 non-Patient subjects also cause R6-to-R4 loss, and generated APIs/search expressions change names and target unions.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R4 arm name strings were removed and replaced by repeating `comparisonGroup` CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: old arm fields are absent in R6; R6 comparison groups can repeat and be coded or referenced, and do not directly encode which group was assigned versus actually followed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Required `ResearchSubject.status` was repurposed from subject lifecycle state to publication status
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the required value set and meaning at the same path changed, so normal R4 lifecycle-status values fail R6 validation; generated enums, filters, and workflow logic also need non-mechanical remapping.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds subject lifecycle and milestone backbone structures not present in R4
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: R6 can carry new lifecycle-history details that base R4 cannot represent, but R4-to-R6 validation is unaffected when the optional backbones are absent.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `ResearchSubject.consent` now repeats
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid for JSON instances that contain `consent`, because object-valued R4 JSON must become array-valued R6 JSON; secondary R6-to-R4 loss exists when R6 carries multiple consents.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
